transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortega (CTO - Lattice Works), Priya Menon (ML Engineer), Samira Khan (Product), Mike (DevOps)

Auto-generated summary: quick intro, qualification, asks about free credits/quickstart, security questions, next steps to start pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alicia from Redwood, AE for this region, um with me is Marcus our SE.
[00:10] Marcus: hey hi all, yeah excited to learn about what you're building.
[00:15] Daniel: thanks, yeah we'll keep this pretty focused, we want to understand how fast we can go from signup to first token and what the cost implications are.
[00:22] Alicia: perfect, that's the quickstart flow we usually show. quick question, who's owning infra for this project?
[00:27] Daniel: that'll be Mike and me, priya is handling model integration.
[00:32] Priya: hi, quick context: we're a team building an internal summarization and search layer for our docs, expected traffic is spiky — maybe 5 to 50 qps — and latency target is around 200-300 ms p50 for short prompts.
[00:45] Marcus: okay good — that's helpful. for 5–50 qps, many customers start on the hosted API to move fast, then either reserve Dedicated when they need predictable throughput. hosted gives you the fastest time-to-first-token — you can sign up, get free credits, grab an API key, and call in minutes.
[00:58] Mike: can you clarify free credits? how long do they last and are they tied to a card?
[01:05] Alicia: yeah typically we provide a trial credit bundle for PLG signups — non-expiring for 30 days after activation, card optional for the trial. Marcus will send the quickstart repo and the sample requests we use for latency tests.
[01:16] Marcus: i'll include a sandbox key and a postman collection, plus a small node/python snippet — time-to-first-token usually ~200-500ms depending on network, but if you're in our nearest region and using small models you'll see sub-200 in many cases.
[01:30] Samira: what's the SDK story? we want product folks to iterate quickly.
[01:34] Alicia: we have lightweight SDKs (python/js/go) plus direct REST. the docs include the quickstart that shows streaming, tool-calling, and embeddings.
[01:42] Daniel: tradeoffs: we're evaluating Dedicated because of data isolation and predictable latency. how different is Dedicated from hosted?
[01:49] Marcus: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and you can pin model versions. you'll get an SLA for latency/uptime and we can do VPC peering for Private deployments if you need complete network isolation. hosted is multi-tenant with logical isolation.
[02:03] Mike: on VPC and KMS — if we need customer-managed keys and don't want data leaving our cloud region, is that supported?
[02:10] Marcus: for Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys; Dedicated can also support bring-your-own-key depending on contract. for hosted we offer encryption-at-rest and envelope keys but not customer KMS by default.
[02:25] Priya: also curious about audit logs and retention — we have compliance audit windows.
[02:29] Alicia: we provide audit logs in Console, you can get token-level traces, and retention is configurable as an add-on. Marcus can send SOC 2/ISO docs.
[02:36] Daniel: ok good. another thing: do you have any benchmarks for throughput with batching? our prompts are variable length, but we do a lot of short queries.
[02:45] Marcus: yes, on batching you get cost improvements but latency tradeoffs. our runtime does continuous batching and KV cache — sorry sometimes speech-to-text says K-V cash — but the idea is prefix caching to reduce repeated tokens. For short queries you may benefit less from batching but we have small-batch profiles.
[03:03] Samira: what's the expected setup effort for our engineers if we start with hosted?
[03:07] Alicia: very small — signup, get API key, install SDK, and run the quickstart. Marcus: we have a sample repo that shows the integration end-to-end — embedding pipeline, storing vect db pointers, and a small streaming example.
[03:19] Priya: do you provide embeddings and vector DB or do we need third-party?
[03:23] Marcus: we provide embeddings API and customers often pair with vector DBs like Pinecone or self-hosted solutions. we don't currently offer a managed vector DB as a core product.
[03:33] Mike: latency stability is critical. if we start hosted and see jitter, can we move to Dedicated mid-pilot?
[03:39] Alicia: yes customers often start hosted then migrate to Dedicated; we also offer burst capacity to handle spiky traffic. migration path is a standard process in Console.
[03:46] Daniel: security red flags: SOC 2 type 2? SSO? RBAC?
[03:50] Marcus: we are SOC 2 Type II, support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC via Console, and can integrate with your audit pipeline. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:59] Samira: and what about pricing model — token-based? and any up-front commitments for Dedicated?
[04:05] Alicia: hosted is usage-based per-token for generation and per-embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers monthly/annual. Marcus will include a pricing sheet showing approximate unit costs and a Dedicated example.
[04:17] Priya: for the pilot, we want to run a 1-week throughput/latency test with ~10k requests per day. what do you need from us?
[04:24] Marcus: sample prompts, expected concurrency and preferred model family (small/med/large), and a list of endpoints. we'll provision a sandbox with keys and a short script to pump traffic.
[04:33] Mike: networking note: we might require egress restrictions and an outbound proxy; will that break the quickstart?
[04:39] Marcus: outbound proxy is okay if you allow traffic to the Redwood API endpoints or use Private deployment. for quickstart you can whitelist IPs or use a short-lived key from CI.
[04:49] Daniel: any gotchas on rate limits? we don't want 429s during burst tests.
[04:54] Alicia: hosted has default rate limits but you can request higher quotas; Dedicated can give guaranteed throughput. we'll note that in the follow-up.
[05:00] Samira: can you send a sample SLA for Dedicated?
[05:03] Alicia: yes we'll attach the SLA doc.
[05:06] Priya: small question: how fast is time-to-first-token for embeddings vs generation?
[05:11] Marcus: embeddings typically return faster since they're single-pass; generation depends on model size and streaming — but for small models we've seen 100–200ms in ideal network conditions.
[05:22] Daniel: ok let's talk constraints: our legal team will need a data processing agreement and to know about data residency (EU region).
[05:29] Alicia: we support EU regions and can run Private or Dedicated in region for residency requirements. legal pack and DPA will be shared.
[05:36] Mike: do you support customer-managed keys in EU region?
[05:39] Marcus: yes, for Private and some Dedicated deployments; for hosted we'd need contract add-ons.
[05:44] Daniel: next steps?
[05:46] Alicia: recap — we'll send pricing, security docs (SOC2/DPA), quickstart repo and sandbox keys. Marcus will provision a sandbox for a 1-week pilot once you share sample prompts and expected concurrency. schedule a technical deep dive with infra next week.
[05:58] Priya: sounds good. is there anything else from Redwood?
[06:01] Marcus: i'll also include a short benchmark checklist and a sample load script. and a note on model quantization/recommendations for cost.
[06:10] Samira: thanks everyone.
[06:12] Daniel: thanks, looking forward to the follow-up.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 6 appeared), some words mis-transcribed (K-V cash), filler words present.
